chapter_title: The Chapter of Fasting, for it engenders a Host of Angels
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by hagiographic dialogue frame and institutional/pastoral material about church office, fasting practice, and accountability. The one quasi-doctrinal claim (“seven angels … by the fasting of each one of the elect”) is inseparable from ecclesial categories (elect/catechumens, lord’s day) and is presented inside a Mani-disciple scene; no self-standing cosmos→cosmos correspondential substrate is recoverable here.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic setup (“Once again… apostle… among the congregation”), direct disciple address, and quotation of what the master said; tightly embedded in church categories (elect/catechumens, lord’s day).
Institutional self-report by a church leader about tenure and supervision of elect; not systematic cosmological exposition.
Quantifying angels from fasting is presented as a church practice audit (elect fasting on lord’s days) rather than an impersonal cosmological mechanism; anchored to community administration.
Continues administrative/narrative arithmetic of angels ‘engendered’ by fasts; no internal cosmic mapping, only institutional practice and personal gratitude.
Anxiety about sinning through commands related to building/ordinance of the church; application voice and institutional responsibility dominate (even where fragmentary).
Supplicatory address to ‘my master’ requesting release from office; classic dialogue petition framing plus institutional role language.
Narrative transition (‘Then, when the apostle had heard…’) describing the apostle’s response action; hagiographic connective tissue.

Begins with a speech-attribution formula (“The apostle says…”) but the content is exhortation/rebuke about seeking exemption and ‘benefit’ of fasts—church-discipline reasoning, not cosmological substrate.
Encouragement to persist in entrusted work; eschatological phrasing (‘land of rest’) serves moral/institutional exhortation, not a structured cosmos→cosmos mapping.
Consolatory promise and motivational speech; strong application voice (‘it will be told to you… I will… so that you…’).
Argument about communal necessity of ‘divine work’ and who will do it; pragmatic institutional concern, not impersonal teaching.
Direct imperatives against asking exemption; explicit second-person governance and office-management register.
Explicit valuation of preaching and ‘building the church’ over private self-edification; institutional programmatic statement.
Addresses fear of sin in speaking about building a church/alms; situational casuistry about church work—late pastoral application.
Moral distinction between commands for communal need vs. for fleshly/selfish need; disciplinary admonition register.
Commissioning/assignment to preach and build ‘the church of God’; entirely institutional and hortatory.
Formulaic closing homage and pledge (‘When that disciple heard… he paid homage…’); hagiographic wrap-up with devotional acclamation.
